method: Dated browser and first-party-page observations for exact HTML-header queue targets. These are access/linkage reviews, not MRF validity or compliance findings. Target hashes bind each review to the original header URL and prevent reuse after a pointer change.

observations.observation: The live first-party page labels a machine-readable file updated 2025-12-08 and links a CSV-shaped cchwyo.org documents URL, but its visible link text is pointer metadata. The link click did not expose verifiable CSV bytes in this browser. The current root cms-hpt.txt was access-denied in the bounded client and browser in the prior dated review, so the historical URL-defense pointer target cannot be treated as a current root-pointer declaration.
observations.next_action: Recover the current root pointer and exact first-party file through a materially different download-capable route or after a publisher change. Compare current pointer target and file bytes before any row promotion.

observations.observation: The live hospital homepage footer labels an uppercase .CSV variant of the Sliced Health /pricer/ URL as Price Transparency. The lowercase .csv URL declared by the current root pointer returned an HTML app shell to the bounded client and previously rendered a procedure-search app in the browser; navigating to the exact uppercase footer link was blocked by this browser. No CSV bytes, facility metadata or update date were recovered from either link.
observations.next_action: Use a genuinely download-capable route or a changed first-party link to recover CSV bytes and facility/date metadata from Faith's exact current pointer target. Keep the existing date-unverified finding; do not call the HTML app shell an invalid MRF.
